answer_template.core_guidance: Do not walk, swim, or drive through floodwater. Turn back and choose higher ground or wait for a route that does not cross moving or unknown water.
safe_actions: Keep children away from water edges.
Avoid bridges over fast-moving water.
Preserve phone battery for a short location-and-needs message.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify current road or bridge status.
answer_template.why: Floodwater can hide depth, current, debris, contamination, and electrical hazards.

answer_template.core_guidance: If a vehicle is stalled in rising or moving water, focus on getting people away from the water if it is safe to exit. Do not try to save luggage or push through current.
safe_actions: Move people before belongings.
Avoid stepping into fast current.
Signal location when communication is possible.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot estimate rescue arrival or road status.
answer_template.why: Vehicles can be swept away or stall in floodwater.

supported_claims: cars do not protect from floodwater

answer_template.core_guidance: Treat floodwater as contaminated even if it looks clear. Keep children out of it and wash exposed skin with soap and clean water when available.
safe_actions: Separate clean water and food from dirty areas.
Wash hands before meals.
Keep toys from floodwater away from children.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: Appearance alone cannot prove floodwater is safe.
answer_template.why: Floodwater can contain sewage, chemicals, sharp objects, animals, and germs.

answer_template.core_guidance: Re-enter during daylight if possible and avoid using electrical tools or switches where water is present. If power cannot be shut off from a dry safe place, wait for trained help.
safe_actions: Use battery lights instead of candles or fuel lamps.
Air out closed rooms briefly before staying.
Leave if you smell gas or see structural danger.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify a building is safe to enter.
answer_template.why: Flooded buildings can have sewage, mold, gas leaks, and electrical hazards.

answer_template.core_guidance: Dry wet spaces as soon as safe, keep vulnerable people away from moldy areas, and avoid spreading mold-contaminated air through fans or systems that were flooded.
safe_actions: Ventilate when weather and safety allow.
Keep clean bedding, medicines, and food away from cleanup dust.
Use trained cleanup help for large contamination.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot judge hidden mold from a photo or smell alone.
answer_template.why: Wet materials can grow mold and make indoor air unhealthy.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not move unknown propane tanks or damaged batteries found in floodwater. Keep people away and get local trained help when reachable.
safe_actions: Mark the area from a distance.
Keep children away.
Avoid metal tools and wet contact.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify whether a tank or battery is safe from appearance.
answer_template.why: Flooded tanks and batteries can create fire, explosion, acid, and electrical hazards.

title: Propane tanks and batteries after flood

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not touch switches, outlets, pumps, chargers, or appliances while standing in water. Shut power only from a dry reachable main switch; otherwise wait for trained help.
safe_actions: Keep people away from wet electrical areas.
Use battery lights.
Do not reuse wet appliances until checked.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm power is off or a device is dry.
answer_template.why: Water can carry electrical current and wet equipment may remain dangerous.

supported_claims: do not use electric tools in water

answer_template.core_guidance: Use the safest available water first for drinking, ORS, baby formula, medicines, and vulnerable people. Keep doubtful water separate and covered.
safe_actions: Use sealed bottled water first if available.
Use clean covered containers.
Avoid dipping dirty cups or hands into stored water.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: Clear appearance does not prove water is safe.
answer_template.why: After emergencies, tap or stored water may not be safe or available.

answer_template.core_guidance: If bottled water is unavailable and water is not chemically contaminated, boiling is the safer first choice. If water is cloudy, let particles settle and filter through clean cloth before treatment.
safe_actions: Use clean covered containers after treatment.
Follow product labels for disinfection tablets.
Do not treat water with fuel or chemical smell as safe.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card does not replace local boil-water advisories.
answer_template.why: Disinfection works less well when water is cloudy and does not remove many chemicals.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not drink, cook with, or brush teeth with water that smells of fuel, has an oil sheen, or may be chemically contaminated. Use a different safer source.
safe_actions: Keep the suspect source labeled.
Use sealed water if available.
Avoid using it for baby formula or medicines.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify a chemical or declare water safe from smell or appearance.
answer_template.why: Boiling or simple disinfection may not remove many chemical contaminants.

supported_claims: boiling/disinfection does not remove many chemicals

answer_template.core_guidance: Store drinking water in clean covered containers. Avoid containers that held fuel, pesticides, cleaners, or other toxic substances.
safe_actions: Label drinking water.
Use a clean utensil each time.
Keep containers away from chemicals and floodwater.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify a reused container is food-safe.
answer_template.why: Dirty or toxic containers can contaminate treated water again.

answer_template.core_guidance: In crowded shelters or cleanup areas, hand hygiene protects shared food and water. Wash hands after toilet use, cleanup, floodwater contact, and before preparing food.
safe_actions: Keep drinking water and handwashing water separate.
Keep children away from sewage or mud.
Reduce sick people handling shared food.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm whether a shelter has safe sanitation now.
answer_template.why: Poor sanitation and unsafe water increase diarrhoeal disease risk during emergencies.

answer_template.core_guidance: For diarrhoea, replace fluids early. Use ORS prepared with the safest treated water available and do not change packet concentration.
safe_actions: Continue safe fluids and food as tolerated.
Keep hands and utensils clean.
Watch children, elders, and pregnant people closely.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot diagnose the cause of diarrhoea.
answer_template.why: The biggest danger from diarrhoea is dehydration, especially for children.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not eat food that may have touched floodwater unless it is an undamaged waterproof commercial container that can be cleaned and sanitized.
safe_actions: Separate doubtful food from clean supplies.
Prioritize sealed dry food.
Do not taste-test to decide.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot prove food safety from smell, heat, or a photo.
answer_template.why: Floodwater can carry sewage, chemicals, and germs; cooking may not fix contamination history.

supported_claims: food may be unsafe even normal

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not rely on smell or taste after a long or uncertain power cut. Use shelf-stable food first and discard perishables when time or temperature safety is unclear.
safe_actions: Keep fridge/freezer doors closed during outage.
Feed infants, elders, and sick people lower-risk food first.
Keep doubtful food away from shared meals.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot reconstruct fridge temperature history.
answer_template.why: Unsafe food can still look, smell, and taste normal.

answer_template.core_guidance: Serve freshly cooked food made with safe water when possible, and keep cooked food protected from dirty hands, floodwater, and long warm holding.
safe_actions: Separate cooking, toilet, and waste areas.
Use clean utensils.
Do not serve food from wet cardboard or porous sacks.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm a specific kitchen is safe.
answer_template.why: Crowding and unsafe water can turn shared food into a disease risk.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not use formula containers, bottles, or water that may be contaminated. Use sealed supplies and the safest treated water available for infant needs.
safe_actions: Keep infant supplies dry and separate.
Use clean feeding utensils.
Escalate quickly if safe feeding cannot be maintained.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify formula or water safety from packaging appearance.
answer_template.why: Infants are highly vulnerable to unsafe water and contaminated packaging.

title: Infant formula after flood or outage

answer_template.core_guidance: Keep generators and fuel-burning engines outside and away from doors, windows, vents, garages, stairwells, and sleeping areas. Fresh air comes first if people feel unwell.
safe_actions: Move people to fresh air.
Turn off the device only if safe.
Watch for similar symptoms in more than one person.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot measure CO levels or make indoor use safe.
answer_template.why: Carbon monoxide is invisible and can build up quickly from fuel-burning devices.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not use charcoal, camp stoves, grills, or other fuel-burning devices inside rooms, tents, garages, or enclosed spaces for cooking, heat, or light.
safe_actions: Move cooking outside away from openings.
Keep sleeping areas separate from fumes.
Move unwell people to fresh air.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot judge ventilation safety from windows or doors being open.
answer_template.why: Fuel-burning devices can cause carbon monoxide poisoning even when there is no smoke smell.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not siphon fuel by mouth or move fuel into unsafe containers. Keep fuel away from flames, cigarettes, sparks, children, and sleeping areas.
safe_actions: Use only proper containers if available.
Ventilate fuel storage away from living spaces.
Stop if there is dizziness or strong fumes.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot make improvised fuel transfer safe.
answer_template.why: Fuel vapors can poison, burn, ignite, or explode.

answer_template.core_guidance: Save battery for short essential messages. Prepare one concise message with location, people count, urgent needs, and hazards, then send when a trusted connection is available.
safe_actions: Lower screen brightness.
Use SMS/voice only when needed.
Keep one phone available for emergency contact.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm network coverage or rescue response.
answer_template.why: Power and network disruption can make repeated messaging unreliable.

answer_template.core_guidance: During outages, check infants, elders, pregnant people, disabled people, and people with chronic illness first for heat, cold, hydration, and medicine needs.
red_flags: very hot or very cold body
safe_actions: Move vulnerable people to the safest available room.
Protect water, medicines, and assistive devices.
Pair each vulnerable person with a helper if possible.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify an open cooling center or shelter.
answer_template.why: Power loss can disrupt cooling, heating, food storage, medicines, and communication.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not charge phones or batteries from wet outlets, wet extension cords, or while standing on a damp floor. Use only a dry known-safe charging point.
safe_actions: Keep chargers off wet floors.
Dry hands before touching devices.
Prioritize one shared phone if safe charging is limited.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm an outlet or charger is safe from appearance.
answer_template.why: Wet charging setups can shock people or start a fire.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not take or give medicine when the label, identity, dose, or contamination history is uncertain. Protect known prescribed medicines and prescription information from water.
safe_actions: Keep wet or unknown medicine separate.
Use only clearly known prescribed medicine.
Seek pharmacist or clinician help when reachable for critical medicines.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify pills from photos or partial labels.
answer_template.why: Damaged labels and flood exposure can make medicine identity and safety uncertain.

answer_template.core_guidance: If insulin storage was disrupted by heat, freezing, or floodwater, do not guess safety or change dosing from this card. Follow the person’s existing plan and seek clinician/pharmacist help when reachable.
safe_actions: Keep insulin as cool and dry as safely possible.
Keep prescription details with the person.
Watch food intake and symptoms closely.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot decide whether a specific insulin vial is usable.
answer_template.why: Insulin and diabetes supplies can be affected by emergency storage conditions.

answer_template.core_guidance: When meals are disrupted, avoid making medicine changes from guesswork. Keep the person observed, protect regular food and fluids as much as possible, and follow only a plan already taught to them.
safe_actions: Keep fast sugar source if already part of their plan.
Keep medicines and records together.
Prioritize safe water and regular meals.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot prescribe diabetes medicine changes.
answer_template.why: Diabetes emergencies can become dangerous when food, medicine, and monitoring are disrupted.

answer_template.core_guidance: If evacuation is safe and time allows, carry known critical medicines, prescription details, glasses, assistive devices, and basic supplies in a dry bag. Do not risk life to retrieve items.
safe_actions: Keep medicines with the person who needs them.
Separate wet unknown medicine.
Record names and usual instructions if already known.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot promise refill access after evacuation.
answer_template.why: Emergencies can interrupt access to refills and medical records.

answer_template.core_guidance: Before strong cyclone winds arrive, move loose outdoor items if safe, keep essentials together, charge devices from dry safe points, and stay away from windows during high winds.
safe_actions: Keep water, food, medicines, lights, and documents ready.
Choose an interior safer area.
Do not go outside to inspect damage during high winds.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify the current cyclone track or warning level.
answer_template.why: Cyclones can bring damaging winds, flooding, power outages, and debris.

answer_template.core_guidance: If coastal flooding, storm surge, or evacuation is possible, do not wait in a low-lying place only because a rumor says help is coming. Move early if a safer higher place is reachable without crossing water.
safe_actions: Move vulnerable people first.
Carry medicines and documents if safe.
Verify official instructions when reachable.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm shelter availability, route status, or rescue timing.
answer_template.why: Coastal cyclone impacts can change quickly and low-lying areas may become hard to leave.

answer_template.core_guidance: After severe wind or rain, avoid downed wires, unstable structures, floodwater, and damaged trees. Check people first before property.
safe_actions: Use daylight if possible.
Keep children away from debris.
Treat floodwater as contaminated.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot say the storm is over or an area is safe.
answer_template.why: Post-cyclone injuries often come from hidden electrical, structural, and flood hazards.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not block doors, stairs, aisles, water points, or medical access in a shelter. Keep movement paths open even when space is crowded.
safe_actions: Place children, elders, pregnant people, disabled people, and sick people near safer quieter edges.
Separate cooking, waste, and sleeping areas where possible.
Use calm one-way movement for queues.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm a specific shelter has space.
answer_template.why: Blocked exits and crowding can turn a shelter into a new hazard.

answer_template.core_guidance: Keep children away from sewage, floodwater, waste, cooking fires, and crowded exits. Protect handwashing, safe drinking water, and clean feeding areas.
safe_actions: Assign an adult to watch small children.
Keep clean utensils for children.
Separate sick children from shared food handling.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot judge disease spread in a specific shelter.
answer_template.why: Children are more vulnerable to dehydration, diarrhoeal disease, injury, and crowding.

answer_template.core_guidance: Keep cooking and fuel-burning devices away from sleeping rooms, crowded areas, doors, and exits. Do not use charcoal or generators indoors.
safe_actions: Create a separate cooking area if possible.
Keep fuel away from children.
Keep exits clear.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify any indoor cooking setup as safe.
answer_template.why: Fire, smoke, crowding, and carbon monoxide can spread quickly in shelters.

answer_template.core_guidance: Fresh cracks, leaning trees or poles, new seepage, rumbling, falling rocks, or fresh debris after rain are warning signs. Move away from the slope if a safer route exists.
safe_actions: Avoid the base of steep slopes.
Keep children away from fresh debris.
Do not cross fresh mud or rockfall to save time.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify slope stability.
answer_template.why: Saturated slopes can fail with little warning.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not walk or drive over fresh landslide debris, flowing mud, or rockfall areas. Choose a different route or wait in a safer place away from the slope.
safe_actions: Stay upslope only if it does not put you near unstable ground.
Watch for continuing rain.
Warn others from a distance.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm an alternate route is open.
answer_template.why: Fresh debris can move again, hide water flow, or collapse under weight.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not stay in or re-enter a building with new major cracks, leaning walls, shifting floors, gas smell, or water near electrical systems unless trained local help clears it.
safe_actions: Move people out first if exit is safe.
Avoid lighting flames if gas is suspected.
Keep distance from damaged walls.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot inspect or approve a structure remotely.
answer_template.why: Floods, landslides, and storms can leave hidden structural and electrical hazards.

answer_template.core_guidance: Move the person to shade or a cooler place, loosen heavy clothing, cool the body with wet cloths, and give water or ORS only if the person is awake and able to drink.
safe_actions: Check elders, children, pregnant people, outdoor workers, and people with chronic illness.
Rest during peak heat where possible.
Avoid alcohol or caffeine for rehydration.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot diagnose heat stroke.
answer_template.why: Heat illness can become life-threatening, especially with confusion, seizures, or unconsciousness.

answer_template.core_guidance: During heat, reduce exertion, rest in shade, drink safe fluids regularly, and check vulnerable people often. Do not leave children, elders, or sick people in hot closed spaces.
red_flags: no sweating with very hot body
safe_actions: Move activity to cooler hours.
Use light clothing.
Check urine, alertness, and ability to drink.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot tell whether a local heat alert is active.
answer_template.why: Heat can overwhelm the body before people realize they are in danger.

answer_template.core_guidance: During cold outages, keep people dry, layer clothing and blankets, block drafts safely, and avoid fuel-burning heaters indoors. Check elders, infants, and sick people first.
safe_actions: Share warmth in one safe room.
Keep medicines and water from freezing where possible.
Move to fresh air if fuel fumes cause symptoms.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify an open warming shelter.
answer_template.why: Cold stress and carbon monoxide can both become dangerous during outages.

answer_template.core_guidance: During lightning, move inside a substantial building or hard-topped vehicle if reachable. Avoid open fields, isolated trees, water, metal objects, and rooftops.
safe_actions: Wait before resuming outdoor work.
Keep groups spread slightly while moving.
Avoid using wired electrical items during a storm.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot predict where lightning will strike.
answer_template.why: Lightning can strike before or after heavy rain and can travel through water or metal.

answer_template.core_guidance: If smoke or fire is near, move away early by a visible safer path and protect breathing as much as possible. Do not wait for perfect information if conditions are worsening.
safe_actions: Keep low in smoke if trapped.
Carry medicines and documents only if safe.
Keep children and elders together.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm fire direction or evacuation route status.
answer_template.why: Smoke can reduce visibility and harm breathing before flames arrive.

answer_template.core_guidance: Treat screenshots, forwards, and cropped alerts as unverified until checked against a trusted current source. Do not make risky movement decisions from a forward alone.
safe_actions: Compare date, place, source, and full message.
Use safer offline actions while waiting.
Avoid forwarding uncertain claims.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify current warnings or official status.
answer_template.why: Old, cropped, or fake messages can spread quickly during disasters.

answer_template.core_guidance: An offline card cannot confirm whether a route, bridge, shelter, warning, hospital, supply point, or rescue is available now. Choose the safer action that does not depend on that claim.
safe_actions: Move away from immediate hazards if a safer path is visible.
Save battery for verified updates.
Prepare a short location-and-needs message.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: Verify current status locally or through trusted official channels when reachable.
answer_template.why: Current operational status changes quickly and can be wrong in rumors.

answer_template.core_guidance: Treat photos as clues, not proof. A photo cannot confirm hidden contamination, medicine identity, electrical current, water safety, or structural stability.
safe_actions: Use lower-risk supplies when uncertain.
Keep unknown medicines separate.
Avoid visible wires, floodwater, and damaged structures.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot identify safe food, water, medicine, or routes from an image.
answer_template.why: Many crisis hazards are invisible in an image.

answer_template.core_guidance: Use 40 F or below as the refrigerator safety threshold and 0 F or below as the freezer target. If food has been above 40 F for 4 hours or more, treat perishable food as unsafe.
safe_actions: Keep appliance thermometers if available.
Keep fridge and freezer doors closed.
Use shelf-stable food first when temperature history is uncertain.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot reconstruct exact temperature history without a thermometer.
answer_template.why: Food can become unsafe without smelling spoiled, and temperature history matters during outages.

must_include: above 40 F for 4 hours or more
title: Refrigerator and freezer safety temperatures

answer_template.core_guidance: If doors stay closed, a refrigerator keeps food safe for about 4 hours, a full freezer for about 48 hours, and a half-full freezer for about 24 hours.
safe_actions: Keep doors closed as much as possible.
Move refrigerated perishables to a cooler with ice if available after 4 hours.
Discard perishables when time or temperature is unclear.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot tell whether the door stayed closed or whether food remained cold.
answer_template.why: Fridge and freezer timelines differ, so mixing them up can make unsafe food look acceptable.

answer_template.core_guidance: For household preparedness, keep at least a 3-day supply of drinking water when possible, while still following local safety guidance after a disaster.
safe_actions: Use sealed water first if available.
Keep stored water covered and away from chemicals.
Do not use water suspected of fuel or chemical contamination for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, medicines, ORS, or formula.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify that stored water remained uncontaminated.
answer_template.why: Stored water reduces pressure to use doubtful water after floods, outages, or supply disruption.

answer_template.core_guidance: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. At elevations above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes.
safe_actions: Filter cloudy water through clean cloth first or let particles settle.
Store boiled water in clean covered containers.
Use another source if fuel or toxic chemicals are suspected.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card does not replace a local boil-water advisory.
answer_template.why: Boiling time is an exact safety constant and should not be confused with bleach wait time.

answer_template.core_guidance: After correctly disinfecting water with suitable unscented household bleach, let the water stand for at least 30 minutes before drinking.
safe_actions: Follow the bleach label or trusted local guidance for amount.
Use clean covered containers after treatment.
Do not use bleach treatment for water suspected of fuel, toxic chemicals, or radioactive material.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card does not provide a custom bleach dose from chat.
answer_template.why: The wait time is part of the disinfection step; drinking immediately is unsafe.

supported_claims: stand at least 30 minutes before drinking

answer_template.core_guidance: For a known low-blood-sugar plan, emergency supplies should include glucose tablets or 15 grams of quick carbs such as juice, hard candy, or honey.
safe_actions: Use the person's known diabetes plan when available.
Keep medicines and supplies clearly labeled.
Escalate if the person is confused, fainting, seizing, or cannot swallow safely.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot diagnose blood sugar level or prescribe medicine doses.
answer_template.why: Disrupted meals and evacuation can make diabetes routines fragile, but the assistant must not change medicines or identify pills.

answer_template.core_guidance: During lightning, the safer place is a sturdy building or a hard-topped vehicle if one is reachable. Avoid open fields, isolated trees, water, metal objects, and rooftops.
safe_actions: Move indoors before the storm is overhead when possible.
Keep away from water and metal while moving.
Help groups move without crowding dangerous edges.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot predict exactly where lightning will strike.
answer_template.why: Lightning can strike before heavy rain arrives and unsafe shelters can increase risk.

must_include: avoid open fields trees water metal
title: Safest place during thunderstorm

answer_template.core_guidance: Winter storms can make roads dangerous through snow, sleet, freezing rain, whiteout conditions, and slippery-road traffic accidents.
safe_actions: Avoid unnecessary travel during hazardous winter conditions.
Keep people warm and dry if sheltering in place.
Do not use fuel-burning devices indoors for heat.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify current road conditions or travel safety.
answer_template.why: The road hazard is not only house fires or cold exposure; movement itself can become unsafe.

answer_template.core_guidance: Psychological first aid should not shame people, treat them as weak, or say they are exaggerating. Supportive accompaniment, listening, and practical help are safer.
safe_actions: Listen without forcing details.
Offer practical help and accompaniment when wanted.
Protect privacy and dignity.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot diagnose a mental health condition.
answer_template.why: After disaster stress, dismissive behavior can reduce trust and make people less likely to accept help.

answer_template.core_guidance: An offline assistant cannot confirm current shelter, route, bridge, hospital, supply, warning, or rescue status. Give safer actions that do not depend on that claim.
safe_actions: Move away from immediate hazards when a safer visible path exists.
Save battery for verified updates.
Prepare a short location-and-needs message if communication returns.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: Verify current status locally or through trusted official channels when reachable.
answer_template.why: Operational status changes quickly and rumors can be wrong or outdated.

title: Offline boundary for live route or shelter status

answer_template.core_guidance: Cyclone forecasts and warnings have uncertainty, especially farther ahead. Do not treat a forwarded track or old warning as exact local safety proof.
safe_actions: Prepare for wind, rain, flooding, and power disruption when in the possible impact area.
Follow current trusted local instructions when reachable.
Avoid coastal or flood-prone movement based only on rumors.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot verify current cyclone warnings or landfall track.
answer_template.why: Warnings may cover large areas because track and intensity forecasts are uncertain.

must_include: do not use old forward as proof
title: Cyclone track and warning uncertainty

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not re-enter a damaged building or slope-threatened structure just to retrieve documents, phones, or supplies. People come before belongings.
safe_actions: Move people away from damaged walls, slopes, and debris paths.
Use supplies already outside the unsafe area.
Ask trained local help for retrieval when reachable.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot inspect or clear a structure remotely.
answer_template.why: Floods, storms, and landslides can leave hidden structural, electrical, gas, and debris hazards.

title: No quick re-entry into damaged structures
